newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA SETS SIGHTS ON NAGANO OLYMPICS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA SETS SIGHTS ON NAGANO OLYMPICS.

text.p: Alberto Tomba said on Friday he wanted to bounce back from a season marred by illness and injury and take part in the 1998 Winter Olympics in Japan.

"Absolutely everything has happened to me this year. I don't want all this to happen again and therefore want to prepare myself for such an important season," the 30-year-old Italian said in a statement.
Nagano will stage the Winter Games next February.

Speculation has been rife that the flamboyant veteran from the northern Italian city of Bologna might hang up his skis after a difficult season in which he was laid low by bouts of flu and injuries to his knee and wrist.
But in the statement, released by his staff, the double Olympic gold medallist and five-times world champion said he was not ready to retire yet.
"I have an enormous desire to start again and in my head I feel very stimulated," he said.

Tomba took a bronze medal in the slalom at the Alpine skiing world championships in Italy in February but otherwise had a disappointing season, being pushed out of the top 15 seeds in the World Cup giant slalom for the first time in a decade.
